terms.comment: Greek διδασκαλικός; ante- and post-classical and rare (Didascalica, the title of a work by Accius; Ausonius): Lewis & Short. Traupman’s word in pellicula didascalica, an educational film. A plain description also serves, in a classical construction: ad discendum ūtilis, useful for learning (ūtilis ad with a gerund or noun); ad docendum aptus says the same from the teacher’s side.

phrases.latin: Hic lūdus et jūcundus est et ad discendum ūtilis.
phrases.english: This game is fun and educational.

sources: Lewis & Short: utilis · Lewis & Short: didascalicus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 52.
